requirement:
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is met. The implementation is complete and exact, and the tests cover the design space.**

**Implementation**
- **Profiles.** Each profile (`src/outline/{rust,python,typescript,css,toml,yaml,markdown}.rs`, with shared `kind_is_comment` in `profile.rs`) supplies an `is_comment` predicate and a `comment_binds_to_container` predicate. The shared `Profile` struct carries both.
- **Markdown.** `markdown::is_comment` accepts only `html_block` nodes that start with `<!--` and end with `-->`. An inline HTML comment is therefore not a comment and stays text of its section.
- **Rust inner doc comments.** `rust::is_inner_doc_comment` binds `//!` and `/*!` comments to their container.
- **Comment collection.** `Builder::walk`, `record_comment` and `record_comments_within` collect comments, including those inside attached siblings such as attributes. `finish` then calls `assign_comments`.
- **Runs.** `assign_comments` (`mod.rs`) joins comments into a run only when all of these hold:
  - they have the same binding kind;
  - neither follows code on its line (`trails_code`);
  - only whitespace lies between them;
  - the next comment starts on the same line as the previous one's end or the line after it.
- **Same-line comments.** A comment after other source, including another comment, therefore forms its own run. `trailing_owner` gives it the innermost node covering that line, using line ranges from before widening.
- **Other runs.**
  - `run_owner` finds the smallest containing node, then gives the run to the next child starting after it, or to the container when there is none. At top level the container is the root.
  - Container-bound runs go straight to the smallest containing node.
  - YAML's `content_end` keeps trailing comments that the grammar folds into a node outside that node.
- **Reference counting.** The downstream requirements use the comment owners:
  - `rust_coverage::missing_function_references` credits a reference to `comment.owner`.
  - `authoring::inputs::reference_selector` uses `owner_at_line`.
  - The `references` and `ripgrep` tools use the same owner lookups.
- **Marking.** All of these items carry `{impl}` markers for `outline_comments`.
- **Unspecified behaviour.** The one behaviour this requirement does not specify is that `assign_comments` widens an owner's line range to cover its comments. The `outlines` requirement and the `selector_raw_lines` example plausibly cover it. I treat it as a minor, defensible extra, since it is needed for `evidence_coverage` of references in comments.

**Tests (`src/outline/tests.rs`, plus `authoring/inputs.rs` and `authoring/tools.rs`)**
- **Run ownership.** `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container` covers:
  - a run before a node;
  - a trailing comment;
  - a comment inside a node;
  - a floating comment with blank lines on both sides;
  - an inner doc comment in a module;
  - a comment alone in a container;
  - a final comment at root;
  - the line ranges of the owners.
- **Next node and container fallback.** The next-node rule, the container fallback, and the root fallback each have a small dedicated test.
- **Same-line comments.** `comment_after_code_on_a_line_belongs_to_that_lines_node` covers trailing comments at several nesting depths. `a_comment_after_another_comment_on_its_line_forms_its_own_run` covers a comment that follows another comment on its line.
- **Inner doc comments.** `file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root` covers `//!` and `/*! */` at file level.
- **Other languages.** `comment_runs_follow_the_same_rules_in_every_language` covers Python, TS, TSX, CSS, TOML, YAML and Markdown. `yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one` covers the YAML folding case.
- **Markdown.** `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` covers the inline versus block distinction.
- **Downstream use.** `references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes` and `search_returns_innermost_nodes_and_comment_owners` check that references and searches use comment owners.
- **Rust item coverage.** `rust_coverage.rs` has its own tests of comment ownership for Rust item coverage.

**Residual gaps**
- Rust inner and outer doc comments on consecutive lines split into separate runs, because a run must have a single binding kind. This reading of "bind a comment kind" is reasonable and is not tested directly.
- No source comments acknowledge any gap, and none is serious enough to fail the requirement.

:::{req} rust_item_coverage

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project: every `.rs` file except those under `.git` or `target` directories at any depth or under the project-root `book`, `evidence`, or `vendor` directories. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, and every struct, enum, and union MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example in a Rust comment attached to it or within its body. Comments belong to items under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; a comment before a field, variant, or attribute inside an item belongs to that item. A named example MUST reference a requirement under {cite}`requirements.examples.definition`. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count for the items it encloses. Habeas MUST report every unreferenced item with its file, line, kind, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When authoring evidence, the edges defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.targets` MUST determine the reference
contributions to the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`. The target of each edge leaving
the assessed subject MUST contribute; sources with only edges into the subject
MUST NOT contribute and remain discoverable under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. A `{cite}` made by the subject
contributes the cited definition's complete fenced declaration. An anchor under
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors` contributes the complete anchored file.
An in-source `{impl}` or `{test}` reference to the subject contributes the source
containing it: for a reference in a supported language, the smallest enclosing
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`; for a reference in a Markdown requirement, example, or
terminology declaration, that complete declaration; for other references, the
complete containing source file. Literal references, evidence copies, and
generated output MUST remain excluded under the existing reference-discovery
rules.
These contribution rules MUST apply only to edges directly leaving the assessed
subject. Including another declaration or source MUST NOT by itself recursively
expand that source's own edges. Reference links MUST NOT be described as proof
that all substantively relevant sources have been found.
